before: description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.
after: description: "Clarify an underspecified software feature or design and capture resolved domain terms and decisions. Use before spec writing when requirements or domain trade-offs remain open. Skip settled specs, routine implementation, debugging, and prose-only edits."

allow_implicit_invocation: false
description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
after: description: "Stress-test unresolved decisions in a plan or idea through focused interview rounds. Use for explicit grilling or as the interview support for grill-with-docs and architecture exploration. Reuse settled answers; do not restart an approved plan."

before: description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.
after: description: "Survey architectural friction and compare refactoring opportunities with before/after visuals. Use for an architecture assessment or refactor candidate exploration. Skip routine bug fixes, a chosen implementation task, and requests only to explain or diagram existing architecture."

before: disable-model-invocation: true

description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
after: description: "Reason about deep modules, interface complexity, and test seams. Use while designing or comparing module interfaces, or to support an architecture assessment. Preserve project architecture vocabulary; do not launch a repository-wide audit for routine edits."

before: Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding.
after: Start from the existing conversation, spec, and decisions. Interview only about material unresolved requirements until you reach a shared understanding.

before: dispatch a sub-agent to find it
after: look it up yourself, or delegate only when permitted by the host and project policy

before: Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.
after: Summarize resolved decisions and remaining questions. Existing approval remains valid; do not ask again for settled decisions. Hand off to the project workflow when clarification is complete, preserving its spec and implementation approval boundaries.

before: Use these terms exactly: don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary." Consistent language is the whole point.
after: Use these terms as an analytical lens. Keep existing project terms, identifiers, and C3 component/service/API names; explain how they map to modules and seams without renaming canonical concepts.

before: Use these terms exactly in every suggestion, and don't drift into "component," "service," "API," or "boundary."
after: Use these as analytical terms alongside the project's canonical architecture names; never rename C3 components or services to fit this vocabulary.

before: Then spawn a sub-agent to walk the codebase.
after: Explore the scoped code yourself, or delegate when permitted by the host and project policy.

before: not "the FooBarHandler," and not "the Order service."
after: while retaining canonical implementation identifiers and service names where needed to locate evidence.

before: Old unit tests on shallow modules become waste once tests at the deepened module's interface exist; delete them.
after: Propose any test consolidation separately. Preserve existing tests unless their removal is explicitly authorized and replacement coverage is demonstrated; the project testing doctrine takes precedence.

before: Tests use an in-memory adapter.
after: Tests use the project-approved adapter strategy and shared contract tests where required.

before: tests provide a mock adapter.
after: tests provide an injected fake or adapter allowed by the project testing doctrine, never a banned module mock.

before: Spawn 3+ sub-agents in parallel. Each must produce a **radically different** interface for the deepened module.
after: Compare materially different interfaces, using the requested count or three by default. Use parallel sub-agents only when permitted by the host and project policy and capacity is available; otherwise develop the alternatives sequentially. Never recurse into further delegation.

before: ADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.
after: Follow the project's existing ADR directory, template, and numbering first. New proposals start as Proposed; mark Accepted only with recorded owner approval. The lightweight template below is a fallback for projects with no convention. ADRs normally live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.

before: description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
after: description: "Actively refine domain concepts and record agreed terminology or decisions. Use when resolving ambiguous domain terms, changing a glossary, or proposing a domain ADR. Skip read-only glossary explanations and ordinary document proofreading."
